chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not befitting for the Muslim to establish brotherhood with the immoral, nor with the stupid, nor with the liar.

key_terms.يُوَاخِيَ: to establish brotherhood or close kinship

ai.seo_question: Who should a Muslim avoid forming close bonds with according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizing that spiritual and social intimacy (mu'akhah) requires moral integrity, not just nominal faith. This hadith serves as a foundational principle in Shia ethics for 'selective companionship,' warning that the character of the three types—immoral, foolish, and liar—can erode one's own piety and credibility. It underscores the practical implication that deep bonds should be reserved for those who embody taqwa and truthfulness.
